title: RBAC Policy Rewind & SIEM Validation — On-Call Runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook describes fast, repeatable steps for an on-call security engineer to: detect RBAC policy drift or unintended privilege changes, capture tamper-evident evidence (audit logs + snapshot), validate SIEM export integrity, and perform a policy rollback (policy-rewind) with minimal blast radius. It assumes RBAC v2 is in use and audit logs emit the canonical schema (see Audit schema summary).

When to use this runbook (triggers):
- Alert from RBAC-drift detector: sudden spike in 'allow' decisions for previously-denied operations.
- User or service account granted a high-privilege role unexpectedly.
- Detection from anomaly model (e.g., new principal performing cross-account operations).
- Direct report from infra team: "we pushed a policy change and observed access escalation".

High-level goals (SLOs during incident):
- Evidence snapshot created within 10 minutes of triage start.
- SIEM export validation complete within 20 minutes.
- Policy rollback validated within 30–45 minutes.
- Communication to incident channel within 5 minutes.

Immediate actions (first 0–10 minutes):
1) Create incident thread: #sec-incident (use template: SEC-INCIDENT-TEMPLATE). Post one-line summary, owner, and initial severity.
2) Triage: confirm alert details (who, what, when, where). Pull the RBAC alert payload and take screenshot.
3) Escalate if high-privilege or production-impacting: @sec-oncall-sre + @platform-leads.
4) Snapshot evidence (automated script recommended). If automation unavailable, run manual steps below.

Evidence capture checklist (automated recipe):
- Trigger: rbac-drift lambda (or manual) creates a secure evidence package in an S3/GCS bucket with restricted ACLs.
- Contents of package: 
  - audit-logs-raw.jsonl (all raw audit entries for the preceding 24 hours + 1 hour future window)
  - policy-diff.patch (git diff between current policy and last committed policy)
  - manifest.json (SHA256s of each file, created_at, incident_id, signer)
  - signer.sig (HSM/KMS signature of manifest)
- Post-process: immutability marker (object lock / vault retention) applied for 90 days or per legal hold.

Manual evidence capture (if automation fails):
- Query audit store for correlation_id and time window. Example Elastic query (KQL):
  - kql: "policy_change OR role_assignment OR rbac_decision:deny OR rbac_decision:allow AND timestamp:[now-24h TO now]"
- Export as JSONL and save to secure bucket with restricted ACLs.
- Capture the policy repo HEAD (git rev-parse HEAD) and generate a patch: git --no-pager diff origin/main..HEAD -- policy/rbac/*.yaml > policy-diff.patch
- Generate manifest: echo -n "audit-logs-raw.jsonl" | sha256sum > manifest.txt etc. Use KMS to sign manifest if available.

Audit schema summary (fields to look for):
- timestamp, request_id, correlation_id, trace_id
- actor_id, actor_email, actor_role, actor_type (user/service)
- action, resource_type, resource_id, namespace
- policy_version, change_type (create/update/delete/assign/revoke)
- decision (allow/deny), decision_reason, rule_id
- source_ip, user_agent, session_id, mfa_present
- raw_payload (compact record of API call)

Key SIEM validation queries (examples):
- Elastic/Core SIEM (KQL-like):
  - "event.action:policy_update AND policy_version:
    * | sort timestamp desc | limit 200"
- Splunk SPL: index=audits (policy_update OR role_assignment) | dedup request_id | table _time, actor_email, action, resource_id, policy_version, request_id
- Cross-check counts: compare raw audit store vs SIEM ingestion for the window. If counts differ by >1%, tag as ingestion gap.

Decision matrix: when to rollback vs patch forward
- If a policy commit is identified as the root cause AND the commit hash exists in policy repo: rollback to previous commit (preferred) if the change is widespread or high-risk.
- If change was a misconfiguration and affects a narrow set of resources, consider targeted revocation of role bindings.
- If SIEM ingestion gap prevents confident forensics, place a pause on automated remediation and escalate to forensics lead.

Rollback steps (policy-rewind) — safe path:
1) Create a reversible change: create an emergency feature-flagged rollback PR in infra repo with the last known-good commit (branch: emergency/revert-<incident>).
2) Run preflight tests: policy-lint, unit-tests, policy-simulation against staging fixtures.
3) Deploy to canary region only (dedicated host) and run simulation queries for 15 minutes.
4) If canary passes, promote to production with a staged rollout and monitor for: denied legitimate traffic, increased 5xx errors, unusual latency.
5) If rollback cannot be applied safely, apply targeted revocations: remove specific role bindings for offending principals:
   - Use API: POST /rbac/v2/role-bindings/remove {principal_id: X, role: Y} and document request_id.

Operational commands (examples):
- Fetch recent policy commits: curl -sS https://config-service.internal/api/policies/rbac | jq .commits | head -n 20
- Simulate policy decision: curl -X POST https://policy-sim.internal/eval -d '{"actor":"user:alice","action":"iam:assume-role"}'
- Export raw audits from storage: gsutil cp gs://rbac-audits/2024/11/20/*.jsonl /tmp && tar czf evidence.tgz /tmp/*.jsonl

SIEM export integrity checks:
- Verify ingestion timestamp monotonicity for the correlation_id. Any large out-of-order events may indicate buffering/backpressure.
- Check normalized fields mapping: policy_version, actor_id, decision must be present. Missing fields -> mapping regression.
- Validate hashes: SIEM export pipeline should add export_manifest.sha256. Compare with manifest in evidence package.

Communication and coordination:
- Post periodic updates to incident thread every 15 minutes until triage complete.
- Notify affected product teams and legal when PII or sensitive scopes are implicated.
- If evidence is being held for legal, apply legal hold and notify GRC.

Post-incident steps (postmortem skeleton):
1) Timeline: record detection timestamp, evidence snapshot time, rollback time, SIEM validation time.
2) Root cause: link to policy commit or automation bug.
3) Remediation: code fix, better pre-commit checks, SIEM mapping tests.
4) Action items: assign owners, due dates, and test plans.
5) Audit evidence retention decision: whether to extend retention, redact, or escalate to legal.

Automation improvement ideas (backlog):
- Real-time RBAC drift detector that cross-checks policy-repo commits + live decisions and emits high-confidence anomalies.
- Built-in manifest signer (KMS) in export pipeline to guarantee end-to-end integrity.
- SIEM ingestion tests in CI that assert schema presence and count parity for representative windows.

Appendix: quick run commands and queries
- Get policy git hash: git -C /repos/policies rev-parse HEAD
- Policy diff: git -C /repos/policies diff HEAD~1..HEAD -- policy/rbac
- Elastic query (JSON body example): {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"event.action":"policy_update"}},{"range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"now-24h"}}}]}}}
- Evidence signing (example): gcloud kms asymmetric-sign --key=rbac-manifest-signer --digest-algorithm=sha256 --signature-file=signer.sig manifest.json

Notes and known limitations:
- If the platform's audit pipeline is down (rare), we may only have partial evidence until service is restored. Preserve what is available and escalate to infra-pipeline team.
- This runbook intentionally biases towards conservative, reversible changes. Avoid broad emergency grants except under CTO-level approval.

Contact list (on-call escalation order):
- sec-oncall (primary): #sec-oncall, rotation calendar
- platform-sre lead: Marco Liu, marco@redwood.ai
- policy-engineer: Priya Menon, priya@redwood.ai
- legal/gcr: Daniel Romero, daniel@redwood.ai

End of runbook. Keep this doc as the quick reference during incidents; link to longer postmortem template and policy repo in linked_artifacts.
